blocks.text: Managing tabs and windows in Chrome for medical coders on mac

Medical coders often work with several windows open at once. You might have your EHR in one window, a coding manual in another, and a claim verification tool in a third. Use ⌘ + N to open a new window for each project. This keeps your clinical notes separate from your billing research.

Inside a window, use ⌘ + T to open a new tab. If you lose track of where you are, use ⌘ + Shift + A to see a list of all your open tabs. This search bar is a lifesaver when you have twenty tabs open for different patient records.

items: ⌘ + L: Jump to the address bar to type a new URL or search query.
⌘ + R: Refresh the current page if a portal seems stuck.
⌘ + F: Search for a specific code or patient name within a long document.
⌘ + Option + Right Arrow: Switch to the next tab to the right.
⌘ + Shift + T: Reopen the last tab you accidentally closed.

blocks.text: Keeping your browser secure and fast

Medical portals require high security. Keep your browser updated by clicking the three-dot menu, selecting Settings, and then clicking About Chrome. Chrome checks for updates automatically, but a manual check ensures you have the latest patches.

Extensions can slow down your browser. Only install what you need for your coding tasks. If your EHR starts acting slow, try disabling extensions one by one in the Extensions menu. You can manage them by typing chrome://extensions in your address bar.

Sometimes a portal will throw an error. Before you call IT, try clearing the site data. Go to the site, click the lock icon in the address bar, and select Site Settings. From there, you can clear data specifically for that site without logging out of everything else.
How to use Lazur to improve your coding workflow

Lazur lives in the notch of your Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask questions about anything on your screen. If you are looking at a complex table in a coding manual, just ask Lazur to explain it. It will read the screen and give you an answer out loud.

You can also use Lazur to dictate notes. Hold the fn key to speak your clinical findings. It types the text directly into the active field in your browser. This is helpful when you need to enter long descriptions into a claim form.

Create a separate Chrome profile for your work. This keeps your work bookmarks and history separate from your personal life. Go to your profile icon in the top right corner and select Add. Name it Medical Coding and pick a distinct color.
You can also pin your most used coding sites. Right-click on a tab and select Pin. This keeps the site on the far left of your tab bar, making it easy to find throughout the day.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur with my EHR?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur works with any app on your Mac, including web-based EHRs in Chrome. It can help you dictate text or answer questions about what is on your screen.

faq.question: Does Chrome on Mac support all medical coding software?
faq.answer: Most modern coding tools are web-based and work in Chrome. Some legacy software may require specific browser versions or settings. Always check your software provider's documentation.

faq.question: How do I fix a site that won't load in Chrome?
faq.answer: Try clearing the cache for that specific site, checking your internet connection, or disabling any ad-blocking extensions that might be interfering with the portal.
